feedback: Written before this robot has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. This is the first iteration, so the feedback rests on the contract alone. The baseline uses a 5-sensor row spaced 15 mm apart, which covers the 25 mm tape across most lateral offsets. The controller therefore relies on the outer sensors to give a usable signal at large errors. The sensor row sits 50 mm ahead of the axle, which gives lead on bends but also means the signal reacts to the line before the wheels do, so the controller needs damping. If the next race shows line loss on the s-bend or slalom, with the robot leaving the tape at a specific curvature, the forward offset or the spacing is the likely constraint. Try a larger forward offset (y = 0.06 to 0.07) first, because it adds lead without changing the sensor footprint. If the race shows steady oscillation on the slalom with no line loss, the track width or sensor spread is the constraint, so try a wider track (0.14 m) to lower yaw response, or a narrower sensor row (x spacing 0.01 m) to reduce the signal gain.
requested_changes: If line loss occurs on the s-bend or slalom: move the sensor row forward, from y = 0.05 to y = 0.065 m, to add lead ahead of the axle, because the baseline was placed at 50 mm with no evidence yet on its lead.
If steering oscillation is high on the slalom without line loss: raise wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.14 m to lower the yaw response, since the 120 mm baseline has no measured yaw behaviour yet.

If the signal saturates or shows dead zones across the tape width: narrow the sensor spread, changing the outer sensors from x = +/-0.03 to +/-0.02 m, to keep every sensor within the tape at moderate offsets.
